RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, November 10, 2010/Kartika 19, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Commerce and Industry; Defence; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Road Transport and Highways; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 20
Production and consumption of
cement
*21. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the annual production and domestic
consumption of cement in the country at
present;
(b) the quantum of cement exported
during the last three years;
(c) whether it is a fact that cost of
construction of residential accommodation
has risen terribly high during the last five
years on account of steep rise in the cement
prices;
(d) if so, details of the steps
Government has taken to ensure the
availability of cement at a reasonable rate
so as to provide relief to the poor persons
who are finding it difficult to construct their
dwelling units; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Eight-point peace initiative for J&K
*22. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that after the
visit of an all party delegation to Jammu
and Kashmir recently, an eight-point peace
initiative was announced by the Central
Government; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
measures being taken for the
implementation of the said initiative?
Pakistani nationals hiding in
Himachal Pradesh
*23. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
increasing incidents of Pakistani residents
'getting lost' in Himachal Pradesh, a few of
them visiting on ground of tourism, visiting
their relations who are staying permanently
in the State, and doing pilgrimage;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that National
Security Agencies have raised the
apprehensions that the Pakistani nationals
with ulterior motives might be using a
peaceful State like Himachal Pradesh for
hiding purpose; and

8
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken by Government to foil such
attempts?
Permission to multinational
companies in retail sector
*24. SHRI A. ELA V ARASAN: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has proposed
to permit multinational companies in the
retail sector in the country;
(b) if so, whether Government has
analyzed the likely negative impact on small
retail vendors in the country;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Delay in completion of EW Corridor
Project
*25. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the East-
West (EW) Corridor Project has been
delayed to a large extent in North East;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for the delay;
(c) the present status of EW Corridor
and steps Government has taken to
overcome such constraints and complete
the project in time;
(d) whether Government is aware that
large scale corruption has been reported in
the plantation of trees and land acquisition
for the EW Project in Assam; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and  the
action taken by Government?
Power of State Governments vis-a-vis
violation of Lotteries Regulation Act/
Rules
*26. DR. T.N. SEEMA: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether State Governments have the
power to prohibit the sale of paper based
lotteries organized by other States/
countries in their State, which are found to
violate the provisions of the Lotteries
Regulation Act, 1998 and Lotteries
Regulation Rules, 2010;
(b) if not, what remedies State
Governments have in case any such
violation is noted; and
(c) whether Government will take steps
to amend the said Act and Rules to give the
powers to State Governments to ban the
sale of lotteries organized by other States
and foreign countries like Bhutan, in their
States, if the operators of these lotteries
are found to violate their provisions?
Resignation by IPS officers
*27. SHRI A VINASH RAI
KHANNA: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that about 80 IPS
officers have resigned from their posts in
the last seven years;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that this
news has been published in a leading daily
Hindi newspaper; and
(d) the steps Government is taking to
deal with this problem?
Legislation to restrict sale of lottery
*28. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has any plans

9
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
to make legislation to restrict the sale of
the lottery in a State which owns the
lottery; and
(b) if not, what are the reasons therefor?
All party delegation to J&K
*29. SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether an all party delegation has
visited J&K to assess the situation of the
State in the recent past;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the names of the leaders with whom
the delegation held discussions; and
(d) the details of the decisions taken by
Government to bring normalcy in the State
after the said visit?
Effect of FTAs with neighbouring
countries
*30. SHRI Y . S. CHOWDARY: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of Free Trade Agreements
(FTAs) entered into with the neighbouring
countries and the impact of such agreements
on domestic industry;
(b) whether Government has kept any
provision for protecting and promoting the
domestic industry in FTAs;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the mechanism of reviewing FTAs
from time to time with the intention of
ensuring protection of domestic
industry?
Steps for protection of acquired land
in Ayodhya
†*31. SHRI JAI PRAKASH: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) the steps being taken by
Government for protection of acquired land
after the verdict of Lucknow Bench of
Allahabad High Court in Ayodhya case;
(b) whether Government has revisited
the issue of deployment of its paramilitary
forces till the time a permanent solution to
the disputed site is found and also of
maintaining the status quo at the site, as
ordered by the High Court; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
India second-most favoured
destination for FDI
*32. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country
is now rated as the second-most favoured
destination for Foreign Direct Investment
(FDI) in the world after China; and
(b) if so, the details thereof in each sector
compared to other countries in the world?
Condition of families of martyred
defence personnel
†*33. SHRI ISHWARLAL
SHANKARLAL JAIN: Will the Minister
of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
machinery at present to conduct periodic
enquiry into the condition of families of
defence personnel killed in military
operations and if so, the details thereof;

10
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) the number of soldiers of the State
of Maharashtra out of the number of
soldiers killed or martyred on duty in the
last five years; and
(c) the details of the ex-gratia /
compensation amount provided to their
families in the State of Maharashtra in each
case?
NHs for high standard improvement
†*34. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT
AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has selected 3,700 kilometre of National
Highways (NHs) for high standard
improvement to bring about reforms in the
road transport in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
names of these roads along with their length,
State-wise;
(c) whether the World Bank has given
approval to meet the financial requirement
for their construction; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the target
of time-limit for completion of this plan?
Foreign investment in highway
projects
*35. SHRI T .M. SELV A GANAPATHI:
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT
AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had invited foreign investment in highway
projects;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that many
investors from China had expressed some
concerns with regard to making investment
in highway projects in India; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps
being taken by Government to address
these concerns expressed by foreign
investors, including investors from China,
in highway projects in India?
New export regulation for pharma
products
*36. SHRI M.V . MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is proposing
to issue new export regulations for pharma
products; and
(b) to what extent the proposed
regulations will help in countering adverse
campaign against quality Indian drugs in
some foreign countries?
Shortage of manpower in Police
forces
*37. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether State Police/CPOs/CBI/IB
suffer from endemic shortage of manpower;
(b) whether IPS Cadre is also facing
shortage;
(c) if so, sanctioned strength and
vacancies in all branches of police, rank-
wise, State-wise, CPO-wise, IPS-wise;
(d) the police-public ratio (policemen
per 100,000 people) in the country, State-
wise, and how it compares with other
countries; and
(e) whether due to shortage of IPS
officers, 16 paramilitary officers from
CPOs had to be posted has ASP in Naxal
hit States though they are not trained for
civil policing?

11
Liberalisation of FDI regime
*38. DR. K.V . P. RAMACHANDRA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
further liberalise FDI regime;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken for accelerating the
FDI in the country?
FIR for carrying out illegal
construction in Delhi
*39. SHRI RASHEED MASOOD:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of persons against whom
FIR has been lodged by the police for
carrying out illegal construction in Delhi;
(b) the names of persons against whom
action has been taken by the police for illegal
construction carried out in Pandav Nagar,
Shahkerpur, Mandawali etc.;
(c) the number of SHOs involved in
carrying out the work of illegal construction;
and
(d) the action taken against them?
Review of bidding process of NHAI
*40. SHRI GOVINDRAO ADIK:
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT
AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
to review bidding process of National
Highways Authority of India (NHAI) by
making it more transparent to achieve the
targets; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 4th November, 2010 Secretary-General.
Kartika 13, 1932 (Saka)
